B.explanation: Follows from $I = V/R = 0.40 \text{ A}$ and $v = I/(nAq)$ with the correct area $7.07 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$.

walkthrough: Find the current in the wire from Ohm's law: $I = V/R = 6.0/15 = 0.40 \text{ A}$.
State the drift-speed relation: $I = nAvq$, so $v = I/(nAq)$ where $n$ is number density and $A$ is cross-sectional area.
Calculate the area: radius $r = d/2 = 1.5 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$, so $A = \pi r^2 = \pi(1.5 \times 10^{-3})^2 = 7.07 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$.

Evaluate denominator: $9.0 \times 10^{28} \times 7.07 \times 10^{-6} \times 1.60 \times 10^{-19} = 1.02 \times 10^{5}$, giving $v = 3.9 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with unit check $\text{A}/(\text{m}^{-3} \text{ m}^2 \text{ C}) = \text{ m s}^{-1}$. This is option B.
